advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the vendor census, when upstream is a plain ModelProfile, assert that its fields carry over to the wrapped profile (e.g. `profile.json_schema_transformer == upstream.json_schema_transformer`); when upstream is None, assert the result equals `BedrockModelProfile.from_profile(DEFAULT_PROFILE)`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_bedrock_vendor_profiles.py:176-178: `assert isinstance(profile, BedrockModelProfile)` / `if isinstance(upstream, BedrockModelProfile):` / `assert profile == upstream` — upstream fields are compared only when upstream is already a BedrockModelProfile

src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:127: `return BedrockModelProfile.from_profile(upstream(model_name) or DEFAULT_PROFILE)` — an added line whose stated contract (docstring lines 114-116) is that the others gain Bedrock fields on top of their own profile

tests/unit/test_bedrock_vendor_profiles.py:155-159: the classify test only asserts Bedrock flag values (all False) and native_structured_output False, which a from-scratch default BedrockModelProfile() would also satisfy
advisory.finding: For vendors whose upstream profile is a plain ModelProfile (meta) or None (unknown vendor), the parametrized census only checks that the result is a BedrockModelProfile. Nothing checks that the wrap keeps the upstream profile's non-Bedrock fields. If the wrap built `BedrockModelProfile()` from scratch instead of calling `from_profile(upstream(...))`, every new test would still pass while meta models silently lost their upstream profile settings, such as the JSON-schema transformer meta_model_profile supplies.
scenarios: A refactor replaces `from_profile(upstream(model_name) or DEFAULT_PROFILE)` with `BedrockModelProfile()` for model_id `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0`. Meta's upstream profile fields are dropped and every test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an else-branch: `elif upstream is not None: for f in dataclasses.fields(upstream): assert getattr(profile, f.name) == getattr(upstream, f.name), f.name`.
